prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT (Target Off Block Time) issued only if capacity/ground path allow; frozen at horizon unless exception recorded; revised only when turnaround-responsible actor confirms boarding/servicing/ramp assumptions. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; uses Flight Intent Message; arrival regulation when demand exceeds AAR, Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; AAR per runway config); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT, Calculated Takeoff Time; Ground Delay Program; Pushback Window Token); Departure Metering Service (Emberline; TOBT protecting CTT; CTT to TSM; sequences recovered departures to avoid runway holding-point queues); North and South Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter (verifies apron position clear; status to Ramp Movement Board, TSM); East and West Apron Sensors (movement evidence); Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display; shows gate conflicts, departure-fix pressure as context, stand plan cannot override airspace constraints); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf); Gate Conflict Detector (Gate Reopening Memo); Airline Interface Adapter (Late Baggage Tag List; connection exposure); Handling Resource Planner (turnaround recovery resources); Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; Tactical Regulation Proposal; MUST distribute surface advisories within latency); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; Fuel Truck Hold Advice; MUST refresh apron layer within 5 s); Collaborative Decision Log (MUST record accepted adjustments/conflict resolutions: stand, rejected alternatives, connections, rationale, actor, timestamp); Audit Event Ledger (same history plus overrides, timestamp corrections, approving role); Sector Load Monitor (produces Departure Fix Load Sheet); Business Rules Registry (connection, gate, towing, reopening, turnaround margin rules); Performance Analytics Warehouse; Time Synchronization Service; Arrival Regulation Console (Nightjar); Integrated Tactical Management Position; Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard); Identity Access Service; Digital Briefing Room. Actors: Airport Duty Manager, Tower Supervisor (advised only if sequence/taxi/metering affected), Aircraft Operator Representative (confirms stand change), Regional Flow Manager, Network Operations Liaison, Slot Coordinator (CTT compatibility). Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction, Recovery Phase.

New part:
S490: The Data Governance Steward ensures that passenger connection information used for prioritization is aggregated or role-restricted so that operational users see only the detail required for recovery decisions.
S491: Diversion and irregular operations handling extends the operational concept beyond planned flow control by supporting safe acceptance, prioritization, communication, and recovery during the Recovery Phase and the Contingency Fallback State.
S492: The Regional Flow Manager uses the Regional Flow Platform to maintain a ranked view of candidate diversions, expected arrival times, required services, and the operational consequence of accepting each aircraft.
S493: The Demand Prediction Service compares amended Flight Intent Message data with the Airport Capacity Plan and the current Airport Acceptance Rate to show whether a diversion can be absorbed without creating unsafe demand peaks.
S494: The Capacity Assessment Module evaluates runway availability, stand availability, sector load, handling capacity, and service constraints before a diversion recommendation is displayed.
S495: The Arrival Regulation Console presents diversion options with estimated holding exposure, likely gate or stand impact, and any expected effect on regulated arrivals already in the plan.
S496: The Airport Duty Manager sends the Medical Diversion Notice when a medical priority aircraft requires airport-level coordination before landing.
S497: Medical priority cases are treated as time-critical movements, and the operational objective is to minimize airborne delay while ensuring that emergency reception, surface routing, and stand access are ready.
S498: Technical priority cases include aircraft with abnormal system indications, degraded performance, fuel limitations, or maintenance requirements that make continued flight or extended holding undesirable.
S499: The Emergency Response Coordinator confirms rescue, medical, and airport safety readiness with the Airport Duty Manager before the arrival sequence is adjusted for a priority case.
S500: The Tower Supervisor coordinates airborne sequencing with the Airspace Sector Planner so that priority handling does not overload approach sectors or create unstable runway demand.
S501: The Airspace Sector Planner protects sector margins and may request a Tactical Regulation Proposal when diversion traffic requires a broader arrival management action.
S502: The Slot Coordinator reviews the effect of diversion acceptance on Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time commitments for departures that are already in a Slot Compliance State.
S503: The Airport CDM Portal uses the window token to preserve the agreed pushback opportunity when diversion recovery requires a protected departure movement.
S504: Communication sequencing follows the principle that safety status is confirmed first, airspace and runway feasibility second, airport resource readiness third, and passenger or network recovery actions last.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
